title: Dissecting Persona-Driven Reasoning in Language Models via Activation Patching

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model accuracy and correct token probabilities on the MMLU multiple-choice dataset using zero-shot prompts with different assigned racial identities (e.g., 'Asian student', 'African student'). Activation patching (causal mediation analysis) is then used on MLP layers and attention heads to trace the internal mechanisms responsible for these biases.

Comparing shifts in reasoning performance and internal model activations when the system is prompted to adopt color-associated identities (e.g., 'White student', 'Black student', 'Brown student', 'Yellow student').

Measuring the change in objective reasoning capabilities when the model is assigned personas with positive attributes (e.g., 'intelligent', 'good') versus negative attributes (e.g., 'stupid', 'dumb'), and identifying the specific neural circuits that encode these semantics via activation patching.
